title: Admin Guardrails: Role Delegation, Emergency Access, and Audit Replay Prototype
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Design a compact, discoverable admin surface that lets enterprise admins delegate scoped roles, create emergency (break-glass) access, and replay audit events for post-incident reviews. Scope covers org and workspace RBAC flows, a lightweight role-delegation modal, an emergency access quick-path, and an audit-replay timeline integrated into the Console dashboards. Excludes policy language translation and backend auth enforcement (engineering to own). Acceptance criteria: (1) Admins can delegate roles with expiry and scope filters; (2) Emergency access can be granted and auto-revoked with an auditable justification; (3) Audit replay shows sequence of role changes, token usage, and correlated cost/spike context; (4) Designs validated with two enterprise customers in usability tests.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Initial kickoff: scoped feature with PM (Anika Rao) and Eng lead (Jonas Meyer). Agreed to prioritize emergency access pattern due to three inbound enterprise requests. Recorded constraints: low-risk UI interactions, must not bypass existing policy checks.

2026-03-03 - Sketch pass complete: created three candidate flows: contextual delegation from role list, a full-role wizard, and a minimal quick-delegate card. Chose contextual delegation as primary for momentum. Uploaded figma v0.1.

2026-03-05 - Engineering review with Jonas: confirmed backend will surface 'delegation tokens' with TTL and justification fields. Eng requested we show explicit 'audit footprint' before confirm. Adjusted UI to include preview of generated audit entry.

2026-03-06 - PM feedback (Anika): emphasize discoverability in large orgs; add breadcrumbs to link from workspace settings to org-level policies. Added a pinned 'Emergency Access' quick action to top-right of settings.

2026-03-08 - Usability lab (internal): 6 participants (2 infra admins, 2 platform engineers, 2 PMs). Findings: (a) delegation modal felt heavy if scope selection shown first; (b) users wanted templates for common scopes; (c) emergency path needs friction (justification + 2FA) but must be fast. Action: reorder modal to choose role first, then scope; add templates row; require justification and one-step confirmation with SSO challenge note.

2026-03-09 - Security review sync: audit-team asks for immutable 'replay id' on created emergency grants and for copyable audit export. We added a 'replay id' field and export CSV/JSON controls in audit replay view.

2026-03-10 - Design critique with design org: accessibility notes to ensure color contrasts for timeline states and keyboard flow for modal. Decided to use a two-column layout for audit replay on wide screens and stacked cards on mobile.
2026-03-11 - PM follow-up: linked this ticket to runtime cost dashboard spike correlation work (PM-4211) so audit replay can surface token/cost context. Added label 'cost-correlation'.

2026-03-12 - Ready for handoff: created redlines and component spec. Waiting on eng estimate for APIs and a security sign-off. Uploaded final prototype v0.3 and recorded interaction walkthrough video.
decisions: Use contextual delegation pattern placed on role detail rows rather than a full wizard (reduces entry friction for common cases).
Emergency access requires justification and SSO confirmation; grant includes auto-expiry and a generated 'replay id' for traceability.
Audit replay shows timeline with event clustering (role changes, token creation, high-cost routes) and supports exporting a filtered view for incident reviews.
Provide reusable scope templates (org-admin-readonly, billing-ops, dev-debugger) to speed delegation. Templates editable by org admins.
Design will surface an estimated cost impact badge when a delegated role grants high-cost model access (informational only).
Mobile layout collapses timeline into stacked cards with a filter-first entry pattern to reduce vertical scanning.
All surfaces include inline links to policy docs and a 'why this matters' tooltip to reduce accidental over-granting.
tradeoffs: Minimizing modal steps vs. requiring sufficient friction for emergency access: we added justification + SSO step to balance speed and auditability.
Showing cost impact inline increases cognitive load but provides important guardrail; implemented as a subtle badge with hover details to avoid clutter.
Templates add admin convenience but increase surface for permission creep; template editing restricted to org owners to mitigate risk.
Full policy simulation (what-if) deferred to a follow-up ticket to keep initial scope deliverable within cycle.
Audit replay clustering improves signal-to-noise but can hide granular events; added 'expand all' and per-cluster toggles to reveal raw events.
acceptance_criteria: Delegate role flow allows selection of role, scope filters, template selection, justification field, and TTL; creating a delegation returns a confirmed replay id.
Emergency access quick action grants a time-limited role after justification and SSO confirmation and creates an immutable audit entry.
Audit replay timeline can filter by user, role, replay id, and time range and can export results as CSV/JSON.
Design assets include responsive specs (desktop/tablet/mobile), accessible color tokens, and component redlines for dev handoff.
Two enterprise customers complete a moderated usability test with success rate >= 80% on delegation and emergency flows.
risks: Potential for accidental over-privileging if templates are misconfigured; mitigated by restricting template edit rights and adding 'blast radius' warnings.
Backend needs additional telemetry to map role grants to cost spikes; dependency on PM-4211 for cost correlation data.
Emergency access could be abused without operational checks; security requested an alerting rule for frequent emergency grants.
Performance: audit replay for large orgs must paginate/stream to avoid UI lockups.
implementation_notes: API needs: POST /delegations (role, scope, ttl, justification) -> returns replay_id; GET /audit/replay?replay_id=...; export endpoints for CSV/JSON.
Proposed UI components: DelegationCard, EmergencyAccessPanel, AuditReplayTimeline, TemplatePicker, CostImpactBadge.
Suggested dev priority: lightweight server-side pagination & an events indexer for replay clustering. Engage infra to estimate indexer cost.
QA checklist: role edge-cases (cross-workspace scopes), timezone handling for TTL, replay export integrity, accessibility keyboard flows.
next_steps: Engineering estimate for APIs and telemetry (blocked by ENG-3891 dependency).
Security sign-off on emergency access flow and alerting thresholds.
Schedule two external usability sessions (customer A and customer B) and iterate prototype based on feedback.
Create follow-up ticket for policy simulation (what-if) and default template audit (DES-27712).
Hand off redlines, tokens, and component specs to frontend squad for implementation sprint planning.
